rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: The JCO prohibits termination of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions for most residential properties not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.summary_plain: In Los Angeles, landlords must have a just cause to evict tenants in most rental properties not covered by rent control, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Los Ángeles, los propietarios deben tener una causa justa para desalojar a los inquilinos en la mayoría de las propiedades de alquiler no cubiertas por el control de rentas, y deben pagar asistencia de reubicación en desalojos sin culpa del inquilino.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978, and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities, short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some government or HACLA-owned properties.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: If you own rental property in the City of Los Angeles, it may be subject to the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO) - Legal Reasons for Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict tenants only for specified at-fault reasons such as failure to pay rent or violation of rental agreement, or for no-fault reasons such as owner move-in or demolition, with relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions.
rules.summary_plain: Landlords in Los Angeles can only evict tenants for specific reasons defined by law, and must pay relocation assistance if the eviction is not the tenant's fault.
rules.summary_plain_es: Los propietarios en Los Ángeles solo pueden desalojar a los inquilinos por razones específicas definidas por la ley, y deben pagar asistencia de reubicación si el desalojo no es culpa del inquilino.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to rental units covered by the JCO in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions_text: Certain property types and uses are exempt as described in the JCO.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: Under the JCO, the landlord may recover possession of a rental unit in specific situations. Below is a list of reasons for which a tenant could be evicted and would be considered at fault... Tenant is not at-fault... owner or an immediate family member will move into the rental unit... Demolition, permanent removal from the rental market, or conversion to non-residential...

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO) - Tenant Protections for Non-Payment of Rent
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict tenants for non-payment of rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.summary_plain: In Los Angeles, landlords cannot evict tenants for unpaid rent unless the rent owed is more than the Fair Market Rent for the unit size.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Los Ángeles, los propietarios no pueden desalojar a los inquilinos por renta impaga a menos que la cantidad adeudada sea mayor que la renta de mercado justo para el tamaño de la unidad.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all rental units covered by the JCO and Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) in Los Angeles.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR). The FMR depends on the bedroom size of the rental unit.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) Rent Increase Limits
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to 5% plus the regional cost of living increase, or 10%, whichever is lower, for buildings older than 15 years.
rules.summary_plain: In California, rent increases for most buildings older than 15 years are capped at 5% plus inflation or 10%, whichever is less.
rules.summary_plain_es: En California, los aumentos de renta para la mayoría de los edificios con más de 15 años están limitados a 5% más la inflación o 10%, lo que sea menor.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to residential rental units in California buildings older than 15 years, excluding certain exempt properties.
rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include units constructed within the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, certain dormitories, two-unit properties with owner occupancy, and some single-family homes and condominiums under specific ownership and notification conditions.
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower.
rules.preempts_note: State law AB 1482 preempts local rent increase limits except where local law is more protective.
